thread_text:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout for release-2026.03.17 started against eu-west-1 (wave 1: 5% traffic). Monitoring enabled. :rocket:
incident-bot: Alert: multiple healthcheck failures in canary group 'rwd-infer-canary-42' — 5xx rate spike to 12% in last 2m. Pager sent to #eng-oncall.
Sally (oncall): I'm looking. Can you post the canary tag + instance IDs?
miguel: tag=release-2026.03.17-canary-42, instances= i-0a1b2c3d,i-0f4e5d6c, lb target group shows 503s from those hosts. Logs show "invalid state: kv-cache-mismatch" repeatedly.
Priya: That KV-cache error matches the new quantized kernel; we saw a regression in perf tests at high concurrency. Rolling this out further is risky.
Ava (support): Any customer impact? CS is seeing error reports from a handful of customers in EU. They're asking if it's an ongoing outage.
Sally (oncall): Assessing blast radius. Miguel, can you flip the safety flag to pause the rollout and revert traffic to baseline?
miguel: On it. Running:
```
# pause rollout
redwood deploy pause --tag release-2026.03.17-canary-42 --region eu-west-1
# reroute traffic
redwood route update --cluster rwd-main --weight 100
```
Doing the pause now.
deploy-bot: Rollout paused successfully for tag release-2026.03.17-canary-42 (timestamp 1778890182). Traffic routed back to baseline variant.
incident-bot: Escalation: Canary abort triggered by policy (5xx > 10% over 1m). Notifying on-call and SRE.
Sally (oncall): Good. Miguel, can you collect a small sample of traces and stdout from the affected instances and upload to the incident bucket? Share links here.
miguel: Uploaded: s3://rwd-incidents/1778889999/canary-42/logs.tar.gz and traces at s3://rwd-incidents/1778889999/traces/ (partial).
Priya: Quick triage — looks like the new kernel's KV eviction path hits a race under bursty requests. Hypothesis: cache index corruption leads to invalid pointer -> 5xx. Root cause likely in the kernel change rolled in this build.
Jamie: Can we hotfix with a config disable for new-kernel? If yes that's faster than full rollback.
Priya: Yes, there's a runtime toggle. Recommend flipping `enable_quant_kernel=false` for canary instances then restart.
Sally (oncall): Action items: 1) Miguel will flip kernel flag on canary hosts and restart. 2) Priya will prepare a rollback build if flag flip doesn't stabilize. 3) Ava will notify customers that we're mitigating and will follow up. 4) Sally to update incident channel on progress.
miguel: Applying flag and restarting now:
```
redwood instance update i-0a1b2c3d --env enable_quant_kernel=false && redwood instance restart i-0a1b2c3d
redwood instance update i-0f4e5d6c --env enable_quant_kernel=false && redwood instance restart i-0f4e5d6c
```
Restarts complete, healthchecks are now green for those hosts. 5xx rate dropped to 0.8% in the last 1m.
Priya: Monitoring traces — error traces gone from restarted hosts. That supports the kernel toggle hypothesis. 
Ava (support): Sending templated customer message now: "We observed elevated errors for a small subset of EU requests during a canary rollout; our on-call team paused the rollout and applied a fix. No ongoing impact. We're investigating root cause and will follow up."
Sally (oncall): Thanks. I'll keep the rollout paused until we have a PR with a revert or kernel fix and we've validated in staging. If 5xx remains low for 30m, we'll do a narrow A/B test with a single host.
incident-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-20260317-1123. Triage level: P2. Linked artifacts: s3://rwd-incidents/1778889999/.
Jamie: Noted. Priya, if you need an emergency rollback, lemme know and I can trigger the rollback pipeline.
Priya: Will do. For now, I'll open a hotfix PR to revert the kernel change and run a fast internal canary in staging.
Sally (oncall): Handing off to Priya and Miguel for mitigation. I'll remain in the loop; paging quieted. If anything flares, page me back. :white_check_mark: 
incident-bot: On-call handoff recorded: Sally -> Priya (mitigation lead). Handoff ts=1778890453.
Sally (oncall): Closing this thread for the initial mitigation. Follow-up actions logged on INC-20260317-1123.
